subject: Post-call: Integration & model-routing follow-up (latency/cost policies, fallback chains)
messages:

Subject: Post-call: Integration & model-routing follow-up (latency/cost policies, fallback chains)

Hi Olivia — great to meet you and the BrightLane team today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so everyone's aligned. TL;DR: Redwood can meet BrightLane's latency and cost targets with a routing + fallback policy, embeddings reranker for search quality, and structured-tool-calling for actions.

Recap of requirements you highlighted:
- Global user base with highest traffic in EU and US; 95th percentile latency target ~350ms for chat flows.
- Cost target: reduce per-utterance token cost vs current provider by ~30% while keeping equivalent output quality.
- Need deterministic fallbacks: primary high-quality model for critical customer flows, cheaper/quantized variant for low-priority/background tasks.
- Embeddings + reranker pipeline for search/faq, with near-real-time indexing (minutes latency) and batched offline re-embeds.
- Structured outputs/tool calling for shipment actions (create_label, get_rate) — must validate JSON schema and allow safe tool sandboxing.
- Auth & compliance: API key + optional mTLS for private endpoints; audit logs required for SOC2.

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Model routing policy by region + latency SLO: route EU requests to EU regions; if latency budget exceeded, fallback to regional cheaper variant or hosted fallback model in adjacent region.
- Fall-back chain example: high-quality model (gpt-xl-8k) -> quantized mid model (gpt-q-8k) -> distilled small (gpt-mini) for non-critical flows.
- Embeddings: VN-embedding-1 for recall + reranker using cross-encoder for precision on top-K. We'll provide batching and caching suggestions.
- Tool calling: structured output with schema validation + Redwood's tool sandboxing for external API calls.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (SDK + auth examples) and integration-arch-diagram.png (proposed routing + caching topology).

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule 60-min architecture deep-dive with Dev (solutions engineer) to go through SDK/auth, region routing, and fallback config.
2) Share a small sample of the typical request/response profile (1k-10k calls/day) and any latency histograms so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted routing.
3) Exchange security questionnaire items (we can start with our SOC2 artifact pack).

Availability: Dev suggested Wed/Thu mornings PST — can you confirm a slot? I put proposed timeline + mutual action plan in the linked MAP doc.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — looping in technical details and a quick SDK snippet to bootstrap the convo.

Olivia — quick technical notes before the deep-dive so we can hit the ground running:

1) SDK & auth
- We provide language SDKs (Python/Node/Go). Auth is API key by default; for Private/VPC we support mTLS and IAM-linked keys. Key rotation and audit logs are available via the Console.
- Quickstart: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key="REDACTED"); resp = c.chat.create(model="gpt-xl-8k", input="Hello")
(see attached redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf for full examples).

2) Region routing + latency SLOs
- Routing policy config (example pseudo-yaml):
  route_policy:
    - match: region == "eu"
      primary: model://gpt-xl-8k@eu-west-1
      fallback_chain: [model://gpt-q-8k@eu-west-1, model://gpt-mini@eu-west-1]
    - match: region == "us"
      primary: model://gpt-xl-8k@us-west-2
      fallback_chain: [model://gpt-q-8k@us-west-2]  
    - default:
      primary: model://gpt-xl-8k@us-west-2
      fallback_chain: [model://gpt-q-8k@us-west-2, model://gpt-mini@us-east-1]

- Policy knobs: max_latency_ms (per-route), cost_threshold_usd_per_1k_tokens, prefer_local_region (boolean), and weight-based multi-model mixing for A/B.

3) Fallback decision logic
- Runtime will evaluate: (a) observed server-side queueing/backpressure, (b) model exec latency percentiles, (c) token cost budget. If any SLO triggers, request is promoted to the next candidate in fallback_chain.
- We can expose a simulation mode to run your historical traces against proposed policies and report expected tail latency and cost delta.

4) Embeddings + reranker
- Use batch-embed API with incremental upserts to our vector store; configure TTL/caching for hot docs.
- Reranker approach: embed candidates (ANN recall) -> top-50 cross-encoder rerank. We support running cross-encoder as a hosted model with pinned capacity for predictable latency.

5) Structured tool calling
- We recommend strict JSON schema validation. Redwood can return schema-validation errors before tool invocation. For safety we support a tool-execution whitelist per route.

6) Data flow & security
- For private deployments we can keep payloads in-customer VPC and integrate with customer KMS for keying. Audit logs show per-request routing decision and which model served each request.

Items I can bring to the deep-dive:
- Live demo of policy config in Console + how to simulate traces
- Sample policy YAML and performance/cost simulation results from similar customers
- Suggested default fallbacks and quantization profiles (to meet your ~30% cost improvement target)

Proposed deep-dive slots (PST): Wed 18 Mar 09:00-10:00, Wed 18 Mar 11:00-12:00. Which works for you?
